name: damped-composite-exposure
rationale: This is lead #1 from the 2026-09-15 report, the pipeline's central open question, and it is the one direction never tested. Four experiments now agree that the composite's realised BAND WIDTH is the damage mechanism rather than its direction: `ta-weight-085-signal-amplitude` (2026-09-13) amplified the composite and lost 14.034 of Sharpe with +7.82pp of drawdown; `family-vote-aggregation` (2026-09-15) widened the band +8.8% and lost 17.447 of Sharpe; `contrarian-trend-subsignals` (2026-09-15) INVERTED the trend family, widened the band 66%, and lost 18.366 of Sharpe — so the composite has measured negative edge in BOTH signs, and every prior experiment moved width upward. Narrowing has never been tried. This hypothesis compresses the composite toward neutral by a constant factor (0.75) before the zone mapping, so exposure tracks a damped version of the signal rather than the signal itself; a factor of 1.0 is exactly today's behaviour and 0.0 would be a static 50% allocation, which makes this a direct, continuously-parameterised test of 'should the composite drive exposure at all'. Honest prediction and its risk: 0.75 shrinks the baseline's realised allocation band (measured 2026-09-14 and independently reproduced 2026-09-15 as composite [0.335850, 0.654840], i.e. allocation [0.295, 0.694] under the current zone) to roughly [0.38, 0.62] wide, which at the 50,000 JPY promotion capital sits close to the ~0.245-of-equity exchange lot floor that already suppressed 5,846 of 5,885 intended rebalances in today's baseline — so turnover will fall and this variant may be rejected on the promotion rule's trade-count criterion rather than on its strategy metrics. That collision is 2026-09-15's lead #2 and is a known structural tension, not a reason to avoid the measurement: the 500,000 JPY diagnostic, where `orders_below_min` is 0, is where the mechanism will be legible. 0.75 rather than 0.5 was chosen specifically to keep the primary-capital run plausibly scoreable.
code_change_summary: Compress the composite signal toward neutral (0.5) by a constant factor before the zone mapping, on both the live and the backtest paths, WITHOUT touching TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's body. Three coupled changes. (1) src/config.rs: add `pub signal_damping_factor: f64` to TradingConfig with `#[serde(default = "default_signal_damping_factor")]` returning 1.0, so every stored config, every existing hypothesis file and experiments/baseline-config.json deserialise to exactly today's behaviour (1.0 is an algebraic no-op). Set it to 1.0 in TradingConfig::default(). Extend TradingConfig::validate() to require it to be finite and within [0.0, 1.0], with a Japanese error message matching the style of the surrounding messages. Confirm the DB round-trip in src/storage/config.rs still works (the repository serialises the whole struct as JSON, so a serde default suffices) and add a unit test that a config JSON WITHOUT the field deserialises to 1.0. (2) src/trading/engine.rs: add one new pure associated function, `pub(crate) fn damp_toward_neutral(normalized: f64, factor: f64) -> f64`, returning `0.5 + (normalized - 0.5) * factor`. Document it with the formula, the fact that the result stays inside [0,1] whenever `normalized` is in [0,1] and `factor` is in [0,1], that factor = 1.0 is the identity and factor = 0.0 pins the composite at neutral, and a NOTE citing this hypothesis and the band-width finding it tests. (3) Apply it at BOTH sites that turn a composite into an allocation target, immediately before `apply_zone`, leaving everything else byte-identical: in src/trading/engine.rs::handle_indicator (around line 387-393, where `combined` is mapped through `normalized * cfg.zone.range_max` into `crate::signal::apply_zone`), and in src/backtest/simulator.rs::run at the corresponding compute_btc_target -> apply_zone site. In both places the damping is applied to the [0,1] composite BEFORE it is scaled by `zone.range_max`. Add unit tests in src/trading/engine.rs covering: factor 1.0 is the exact identity for several values; factor 0.0 returns 0.5 for any input; factor 0.75 maps 0.654840 and 0.335850 (the measured baseline band edges) to values strictly closer to 0.5 while preserving their side of neutral; and the output stays within [0,1] at the input extremes 0.0 and 1.0. In your report, instrument and state the realised composite band (min/max/sd) for BOTH the baseline formula and the damped one over the identical evaluated candles, per the 2026-09-15 cross-validation practice, plus `orders_below_min` at all three capitals so the turnover drop is attributable to the lot floor versus the threshold.
constraints: MUST NOT change TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's signature (its parameter list or return type) or its body — the damping is applied to that function's RESULT at the call sites, so the composite formula itself is held fixed and the measured effect is attributable to the compression alone.

MUST apply the damping at BOTH call sites (the live site in src/trading/engine.rs::handle_indicator and the backtest site in src/backtest/simulator.rs::run), so the backtest cannot measure a strategy the live engine would not run. Leaving the live path unchanged would make the backtest result meaningless.

MUST default `signal_damping_factor` to 1.0 via serde and in TradingConfig::default(), so a stored config or a hypothesis file lacking the field behaves exactly as today. The baseline run must remain byte-identical to a run of the unmodified code — verify this explicitly and say so in your report.

MUST NOT change TradingEngine::allocation_delta_to_order, the allocation_threshold comparison at any call site, apply_zone, the sticky_target logic, the RiskManager call sequence, the exchange lot-size check, the fee logic, or the orders_below_min counting arm.

MUST pass `cargo test`, including the existing compute_btc_target_* tests in src/trading/engine.rs and the simulator tests in src/backtest/simulator.rs — update an expected value only where the new field legitimately changes it (do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass).

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically — a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff changes the allocation target on the LIVE order-submission path, per the 'anything touching live trading behavior gets flagged explicitly' rule in docs/self-improvement-loop.md.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or the bitFlyer REST/WS client.
